title: The Burning Oath Revisited
premise: Juniper Halloran has spent five years hiding in the city of Vell, selling harmless charms while pretending the sealed gate beneath their shop is nothing but old stone. When a mute child named Ash arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Juniper realizes the child's soul was sold to the Undercourt beneath the mountain—and that Juniper themselves made the bargain years ago to save someone they loved, then erased the memory. To free Ash, Juniper must cross into the court of the buried dead, confront the version of themselves who signed the oath, and choose between restoring their lost memories and keeping the child whole. In the end, Juniper reclaims the truth at terrible cost, breaks the burning oath, and builds a new kind of family from the pieces left behind.
about_author: Oscar Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal cities before turning to fiction. They write about gates, bargains, and the families we assemble when the old ones fail us.

chapters.title: The Shop of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A day in the charm shop establishes Vell's anti-magic laws, Juniper's careful invisibility, and the sealed gate in the cellar they refuse to look at. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: A Knock in Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On a storm night, a child arrives barefoot, unable to speak anything but a language Juniper somehow half-understands. The gate in the cellar hums for the first time in five years. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Charms Cannot Do
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper tries mundane remedies for Ash's muteness and nightmares; every charm fails except one that answers back. A neighbor, the widow Sera, notices too much. Emotional beat: the mask beginning to slip.

chapters.title: The Language Beneath Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Ash's POV, rendered as impressionistic fragments. The child remembers a mountain, a hall of candles, and hands signing away something precious. Emotional beat: terror without vocabulary.

chapters.title: Sera Knows
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Sera confronts Juniper—not with betrayal, but with an offer of help; she once lost a sister to the Undercourt. First hint that others remember what Juniper cannot. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Sold Souls
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the city archives, Juniper finds a ledger listing souls bought by the court beneath the mountain—Ash's name beside a signature Juniper recognizes as their own handwriting. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Five Years Missing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper interrogates their own past: a gap where memories should be, a scar shaped like a seal, a half-burned oath paper hidden in the floorboards. Emotional beat: grief for a self they can't recall.

chapters.title: The Gate Wakes
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Drawn downstairs by the humming, Ash touches the cellar gate and it opens a crack; something on the other side whispers Ash's true name. Juniper slams it shut. Emotional beat: the past refusing containment.

chapters.title: Hunters in Fine Coats
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Agents of the Magistry arrive asking about unlicensed magic; Sera covers for them, but the visit makes clear time is short. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Widow
chapters.summary: Juniper and Sera's shared POV chapters alternate. Sera reveals the road to the mountain and the price of entry: a memory freely given at each threshold. Emotional beat: trust built through mutual damage.

chapters.title: Leaving Vell
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper closes the shop, leaves the key with a neighbor, and sets out with Ash at dawn as Magistry watchers follow. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The old pilgrim road stirs forgotten things; Juniper begins recovering flashes—the person they loved, the night of the bargain. Ash grows bolder, teaching Juniper words. Emotional beat: found family taking root.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Memories
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the first threshold, Juniper pays a memory—the taste of their mother's kitchen—and feels how much the court values what we overlook. Emotional beat: sacrifice as currency.

chapters.title: Voices in the Snowline
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Higher on the mountain, the dead call to Ash in their native tongue, offering warmth if Ash stops resisting. Juniper anchors them with a simple charm bracelet. Emotional beat: love as lifeline.

chapters.title: The Second Threshold
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The toll demanded now is larger: the face of the person Juniper saved five years ago. Juniper pays it and immediately mourns someone whose name is already gone. Emotional beat: heartbreak without an object.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Descent into the candlelit Undercourt, where the Buried King keeps souls in jars of amber light and speaks courteously of contracts. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Other Juniper
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the court's mirror-hall stands the self who signed the oath—younger, desperate, unrepentant—who explains why the bargain was made and warns against paying the final toll. Emotional beat: confrontation with one's own motives.

chapters.title: The Burning Oath
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The final threshold demands everything: restore all memories and keep the oath intact, or remain hollow and break it. Juniper chooses memory, reliving the night they sold Ash's soul to save their dying partner—and understands both selves. Emotional beat: devastating clarity.

chapters.title: Breaking the Contract
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Armed with full memory, Juniper exploits a flaw in the oath—it was sworn by a self who no longer exists—and burns it before the Buried King, shattering the amber jars. Emotional beat: defiant triumph amid chaos.

chapters.title: The King's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Climax. The Buried King offers Juniper restoration of their partner in exchange for Ash; Juniper refuses, and the collapsing court forces a flight up the mountain with Ash's soul flickering between them. Emotional beat: choosing the living over the lost.

chapters.title: Dawn Over Vell
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper and Ash return to a changed city; the gate in the cellar crumbles to ordinary stone. Ash speaks their first word in common tongue: Juniper's name. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Open Doors
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Juniper's POV. Months later, the shop sells real magic again, quietly, to those who need it; Sera is family now, and other lost children find the door. Juniper keeps no oaths—only promises. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.
